text: What is the difference between var, let and const in JavaScript?
key_points: var is function scoped and can be redeclared|let is block scoped and can be reassigned but not redeclared|const is block scoped and cannot be reassigned|a const object can still have its contents changed

text: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
key_points: == compares after converting types (coercion)|=== compares value and type with no conversion|5 == '5' is true but 5 === '5' is false|prefer === to avoid surprises

text: What is hoisting, and what is the Temporal Dead Zone?
key_points: declarations are registered before code runs|var is hoisted and starts as undefined|let and const are hoisted but cannot be used before their line (TDZ)|touching them early throws a ReferenceError

text: What is a closure in JavaScript, and why is it useful?
key_points: a function remembers the variables of the scope it was created in|still works after the outer function has returned|gives private data, for example a counter or bank balance|each call of the outer function makes separate private state

text: What do map, filter and reduce do, and how are they different?
key_points: map transforms every element into a new array of the same length|filter keeps only elements that pass a test|reduce folds the array into one value using an accumulator|none of them change the original array

text: How does JavaScript handle asynchronous work even though it is single-threaded?
key_points: the call stack runs one thing at a time|timers and network calls are handled by browser or Node APIs in the background|finished callbacks wait in a queue|the event loop moves them to the stack when it is empty

text: Why does a promise callback usually run before a setTimeout callback with zero delay?
key_points: promise callbacks go to the microtask queue|timer callbacks go to the callback (macrotask) queue|the event loop empties microtasks before taking the next timer callback|so then() runs first even though the timer was set earlier

text: What is a promise, and how does async await relate to it?
key_points: a promise stands for a value that will arrive later: pending, fulfilled or rejected|then and catch handle success and failure|async await is cleaner syntax over promises|errors are handled with try catch around await

text: How do cookies, localStorage and sessionStorage differ?
key_points: cookies are small and sent to the server with every request|localStorage stays until it is cleared and is not sent to the server|sessionStorage is cleared when the tab closes|do not keep secrets in localStorage

text: You copy an object with the spread operator, change a nested value on the copy, and the original changes too. Why?
key_points: spread makes a shallow copy|nested objects are copied by reference, so both share them|a deep copy duplicates the nested parts as well|structuredClone is one way to deep copy; JSON round trip loses functions

text: A long list gets new items added later, and each item must respond to clicks. How would you handle the clicks efficiently?
key_points: event delegation: one listener on the parent|clicks bubble up from the item to the parent|check event target to find which item was clicked|works for items added later without new listeners

text: You need a counter that keeps its count private and gives every user their own separate counter. How would you build it?
key_points: a function that declares the count inside and returns an inner function|the inner function closes over the count|each call creates an independent counter|no global variable that others could change

text: What is Node.js, and why can JavaScript run on a server with it?
key_points: a runtime that runs JavaScript outside the browser|built on the V8 engine|non-blocking event-driven input and output|npm gives a large ecosystem of packages

text: What is middleware in Express, and where does it sit in a request?
key_points: a function with request, response and next|runs between the incoming request and the route handler|can change the request, end the response or call next|order of app.use matters; examples are logging, parsing, authentication

text: What is the MVC pattern, and how does it organise a backend project?
key_points: model holds data and database logic|view is what the user sees|controller handles the request logic|routes connect URLs to controllers; keeps code easier to maintain

text: What is the difference between server-side rendering and client-side rendering?
key_points: server-side: the server builds the full HTML page|client-side: the browser builds the page with JavaScript from data|server-side gives faster first paint and better search visibility|client-side feels smoother after the first load

text: How is MongoDB different from a relational database?
key_points: stores documents (JSON-like) instead of table rows|collections instead of tables|flexible schema|the M in the MERN and MEAN stacks

text: What is Mongoose, and what do a schema and a model do?
key_points: an ODM library for MongoDB and Node|schema defines the structure and validation of documents|model is the wrapper used to query and save|stops bad data before it reaches the database

text: How do cookies and sessions work together to keep a user logged in?
key_points: server sends a Set-Cookie header with a session id|browser sends the cookie back on each request|session data stays on the server|only the id travels in the cookie, not the user data

text: What is the difference between authentication and authorization, and where would you enforce each?
key_points: authentication checks who you are, for example login|authorization decides what you may do|authentication comes first, then authorization|enforce both on the server, for example in middleware on protected routes

text: Why should passwords be hashed instead of stored as plain text or encrypted?
key_points: if the database leaks, plain passwords are exposed|a hash is one-way, encryption can be reversed|a salt stops precomputed lookup tables|login compares the hash of the attempt with the stored hash

text: In an Express route, req.body is undefined. How would you find and fix the cause?
key_points: body parsing middleware is missing|express.json for JSON and express.urlencoded for form data|check the Content-Type header matches|register the middleware before the routes; multer for file uploads

text: A user logs in successfully, but the very next request says they are not logged in. How would you investigate?
key_points: check the Set-Cookie header reached the browser|check the browser sends the cookie back (domain, path, secure flags)|check session middleware is set up before the routes|check the server still has the session (restart, store)

text: What is the virtual DOM, and why does React use it?
key_points: a lightweight JavaScript copy of the real DOM|React compares the old and new versions (diffing)|only the changed parts of the real DOM are updated|cheaper than rebuilding the whole page

text: What is the difference between props and state in React?
key_points: props are passed down from a parent and are read-only|state belongs to the component and can change|a state change causes a re-render|share state by lifting it up to a common parent

text: Why do items in a rendered list need a key in React?
key_points: a unique, stable identifier among siblings|lets React match items between renders|avoids wrong updates when the list is reordered or filtered|array index is a poor key when the list changes

text: What does the dependency array of useEffect control?
key_points: the effect re-runs when a listed value changes|an empty array runs it once after the first render|no array runs it after every render|a missing dependency can cause stale values

text: What is debouncing, and how does the cleanup function in useEffect help implement it?
key_points: wait until the user stops typing before running the work|the effect starts a timer on each change|cleanup clears the previous timer|cleanup also removes listeners, intervals and cancels requests

text: Your component pushes a new item into an array held in state, but the screen does not update. Why, and how do you fix it?
key_points: push changes the same array, so React sees no new reference|create a new array, for example with the spread operator|use the functional update: set(prev => [...prev, item])|never mutate state directly

text: A user opens a link like /products/101 directly in the browser on your React app and the server returns not found. What is happening?
key_points: React Router handles paths in the browser, not on the server|a direct request goes to the server, which has no such file|configure the server to fall back to index.html|inside the app use Link instead of plain anchors
